claim: Saturn's rings reach up to 282,000 km from the planet, yet the main rings are typically only about 10 m (30 ft) thick.

beats.caption: How wide?
beats.vo: They reach up to 282,000 kilometers from the planet.

beats.caption: How thick?
beats.vo: But the main rings are typically only about 10 meters thick.

beats.caption: Not solid
beats.vo: And they're not solid. They're billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust specks to house-sized boulders.

beats.caption: Edge-on
beats.vo: Turn Saturn edge-on, and the rings nearly vanish.

beats.caption: Scale it down
beats.vo: Shrink the rings to one kilometer wide, and they'd be thinner than a sheet of paper.

beats.caption: Wide as a world
beats.vo: Wide as a world. Thin as a house.

sources.text: NASA Science, Saturn Facts: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ (ring system extends up to 175,000 mi / 282,000 km; vertical height typically about 30 ft / 10 m in the main rings; ring particles from dust-sized grains to house-sized chunks)
